You are a Python 3.12 engineer building an offline-first probe harness for freytag-forge, approved by Brandon. Working directory: /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge (branch 1a-opening-and-truck-feedback). Environment: no uv. Run `export PYTHONPATH=/home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge TMPDIR=/tmp CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_URL=https://w.example` then `.venv/bin/python`. NEVER make a real network call or a billed call: every test and your own checks must stub the network. Do not git commit.

YOU MAY CREATE OR EDIT ONLY: scripts/ringer/opening_truck/probe.py and tests/test_opening_truck_probe.py (both new). Never edit storygame/, packages/, data/, docs/, bench/, .plans/, or any existing script or test. Read-only references you may import from or copy patterns from: scripts/ringer/transcript_1a/boarding_probe.py (CallCounter, QuotaExceeded, CallCapExceeded, _send_narrator, _quota_code, _narration_from_reply, _write_json, _jsonable; tests/test_boarding_probe.py shows how it is tested) and .plans/1a-opening-and-truck-feedback/capture.py (a working network-free, product-wired replay that attaches WorldCapture with a scripted question-answerer; copy its approach, do not import it). The preregistration you implement is .plans/1a-opening-and-truck-feedback/probe1-prereg.md: read it first; this spec restates what you build.

WHAT TO BUILD, scripts/ringer/opening_truck/probe.py, CLI `python scripts/ringer/opening_truck/probe.py (--dry | --smoke | --run) --out PATH [--max-calls N] [--confirm]` (default max-calls 85):
1. build_document(): offline, no network. Builds (a) the shipped 1A OPENING narrator request (system, user) from the product-wired provider on the continuity-initiative package (data/stories/continuity-initiative); (b) the Part 2 control request: replay the route 'open the drawer', 'feel in the gap' then the command 'head out to the truck' through RuntimeEngine with WorldCapture attached, Jev scripted so boards_vehicle is yes and only_boards_vehicle is yes for a command naming the truck, the network stubbed, and keep the narrator request sent on the boarding turn; (c) arm 1 = the control request whose PLAYER block has the line equal to '- head out to the truck' removed, system text and every other line byte-identical (assert this and record a unified diff); (d) the Part 1 call list. Validate the control: it must contain 'Already done:' and the raw command line and a SCENE line saying she is in the driver's seat; raise a clear error if not.
2. Part 1 plan (live Jev): boards_vehicle for 8 phrasings x 2 vehicle names x 2 samples = 32 calls, phrasings with a {v} slot: 'head out to {v}', 'go out to {v}', 'go to {v}', 'get in {v}', 'climb into {v}', 'walk up to {v}', 'look at {v}', 'get out of {v}'; vehicle names "Kristin's truck" and "the van" (so 'head out to Kristin's truck' / 'head out to the van'; for the truck use 'the truck' in the command text and "Kristin's truck" as the vehicle_name argument; for the van use 'the van' in both). Plus only_boards_vehicle for the first four phrasings on the truck only, 2 samples = 8 calls. Use storygame.runtime.jev_questions.boards_vehicle_payload / only_boards_vehicle machinery and storygame.runtime.jev.JevClient.from_environment().ask for the live path (read those modules; the live answer is a noul probability, yes means greater than jev.THRESHOLD via noul_yes). Record per call the command, vehicle name, question, raw answer object, the boolean from noul_yes (None when unanswered) and any error. Count each ask as one call against the cap.
3. Part 2 plan (live narrator): 12 samples of control and 12 of arm 1, interleaved (control, arm1, control, ...). Part 3 plan: 10 samples of the opening request. Send via a narrator sender with the same headers, auth, quota detection, timeout and parsing as boarding_probe._send_narrator (reuse it by import).
4. Totals: 40 + 24 + 10 = 74 calls. The cap check must run before the first call and refuse if the planned total exceeds --max-calls. --dry writes the document (prompts, diff, plan, totals) and makes zero calls. --smoke is billed and needs --confirm: exactly 3 Jev calls (one 'head out to' boards_vehicle truck, one 'get in' boards_vehicle truck, one 'walk up to' boards_vehicle truck), 1 control narrator call and 1 opening call (5 total). --run is billed and needs --confirm and runs the full 74. Without --confirm any billed mode must exit non-zero with a message and make no call. Stop immediately and keep partial rows on a 429 or on AI_QUOTA_EXCEEDED / AI_DAILY_BUDGET_EXCEEDED (reuse the boarding_probe logic). No retries, no replacement samples. Write the result JSON after every call so a crash keeps rows. Output is a rows list plus mode, calls_made, stop_reason and the document hash.
5. Guard: refuse to run a billed mode when CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_URL is empty or equals the placeholder https://w.example.

TESTS FIRST in tests/test_opening_truck_probe.py (hermetic; fail the test if any real urlopen or socket is reached: monkeypatch storygame.runtime.cloudflare.urlopen and JevClient ask to fakes): the dry document has the arm 1 diff removing exactly one line and nothing else; the control contains the required markers; the plan totals 74 (40/24/10) and the cap check rejects --max-calls 73; billed modes without --confirm exit non-zero with zero calls; the placeholder URL is refused; a fake narrator and fake Jev drive a full --run to 74 recorded rows with the expected interleaving and answer parsing (including a None answer); a fake 429 quota reply stops the run and keeps partial rows; --smoke makes exactly 5 calls. Also assert no module-level network side effects on import.

DONE WHEN the check passes. Report which existing helpers you imported and anything you could not do.
